placement.position_note: Interpretive placement on a GENERATED lot, not a recovered parcel. The lot geometry is the K7 plat module's — this project has never read Thompson's numbering off a sheet, and the side lot lines and the alley are conjectural even where the block face is not. The building stands 4.0 m back from its street edge, which is a typology for the period and not a measurement of this lot. The whole footprint — not its centre — is tested against the platted street corridors, against its own lot lines and against every other footprint in the dataset, so no invented building of this parcel stands in the roadway; clearing the roadway is not the same as standing on a recovered lot.

persons.name: Elias S. Dykine
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Dykine, Elias S.' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). persons.name: Samuel E. Toby
persons.note: GRADED BY THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER — rule G3, applied 2026-09-04. This identity is inferred because that rung fired on the civic and press rows recorded on this card, which the resident-research corpus does not read. This programme's letter-list rule of 2026-09-02 would call it a projected resident on the absence of a research row; it is superseded here, and a no-find in one corpus is not a finding about another (T-0822). KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN PRINTED THREE TIMES. The return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office on 1 July 1834 was set three times in the Chicago Democrat — 1834-07-02 p3 c2, 1834-07-09 p1 c2 and 1834-07-16 p1 c2 — and two of those settings print 'samuel E. Toby' where the middle one prints 'samuel. Toby' and sets no middle initial at all. THE OWNER RULED ON 2026-09-24 (T-1528) that a present initial may absorb an ABSENT one at the same entry of the same list, bounded exactly as T-0392's unread-initial ruling was, and the gazetteer now keys this person on 'Samuel E. Toby' — the reading that carries every letter a printing set, which tools/compile_gazetteer.py refuses to let a merge discard. THIS CARD WEARS THAT READING (T-1561). It displayed 'Samuel. Toby' until then, which is the ABSORBED side: after the merge, nothing this record cites read the name that way, and the surviving reading was sitting in this card's own press_evidence row. THE ID DOES NOT MOVE WITH THE NAME — `toby_samuel` is a handle every crosswalk cites and not a claim (rule N5, T-1139), and the family name it was minted off is the one the card still reads. AND THE FIELD NOW FOLLOWS THE MERGED RECORD (T-1562). `letter_list_returns` is one date PER RETURN and not per printing, so three impressions of the 1 July 1834 return put ONE date in it, and it is the first printing that carries the name: 1834-07-02. It held the 1834-07-09 impression until then, which was neither the first printing nor the last but the issue one extraction crop reached. Reading the last printing in instead would date the evidence by a compositor's re-run; carrying both ends would say the office held letters for this man in two separate returns, which is the strongest thing a letter list can say about residence and is not what happened. THE ARRIVAL BLOCK DID NOT MOVE — it is dated by the return and never by the impression (T-0425), so it read 1834-07-01 while the earliest printing behind the name was still eight days late, and it reads 1834-07-01 now. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.
